title: OpenAI's Human Rights Chief Warns 'Everyone Is Very Worried' About AI In Armed Conflicts
source_used: Fortune (first reporter of the on-stage remarks); Benzinga copy blocked (403)
key_facts: Sarah Yager became OpenAI's first human rights and responsible deployment lead in June 2026, focused on military applications.
She spoke on stage on Tuesday, 6 Oct 2026, at the ScaleUp:AI conference in New York City.
She said: 'This keeps me up at night: What is the military going to do with AI when it comes to targeting? And what about autonomous weapons?'
OpenAI signed a contract with the Department of War in late February to deploy advanced AI in classified environments, after the department labelled Anthropic a supply-chain risk.
She said human rights should be the baseline for military AI and that she worked with engineers so models give appropriate responses to the laws of war.
She said she is helping oversight bodies such as the Government Accountability Office build tools to track government AI use.
quote_evidence: "Everyone is very worried and rightly so," Yager said.
"I do not want an AI company telling me what is good. If we allow the industry to determine what is good, then it’s a free-for-all."
why_it_matters_hint: OpenAI's own human rights lead says military targeting and autonomous weapons are a serious worry for AI firms.
